test_title: PYST 28: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - General Awareness (Held On: 21th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Regarding the Inter-State Council (ISC), which of the following is/are correct?

A) It is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.

B) It mainly gives recommendations and is not a judicial body for settling disputes.

options.text: Both A and B are correct
Neither A nor B is correct

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Inter-State Council (ISC) is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**. This is as per Article 263 of the Indian Constitution, which provides for such a council to discuss and recommend on matters of inter-state disputes and coordination.
 
• It is a **recommendatory body** and does not have judicial or binding powers. Its role is limited to providing advice and facilitating coordination between states and the center.
 
• The council can discuss and investigate subjects of common interest between the central and state governments and make recommendations for better policy coordination.
 
• The ISC was **constituted in 1990** based on the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission, which was set up to review center-state relations.
 
• The council includes Chief Ministers of all states, Union Territories with legislative assemblies, and administrators of Union Territories, along with six Union Ministers and other representatives, depending on the agenda of the meeting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Details about Article 263 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 263 provides the President of India the power to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears to him/her that public interests would be served by its establishment.
 
• The ISC is designed to serve as a forum for discussing and addressing issues related to inter-state and center-state relations.
 
• It is not a permanent constitutional body and can be set up whenever necessary to address specific issues.
 
 
 
• **Difference between ISC and Zonal Councils:**
 
 
• While the ISC deals with broader inter-state and center-state issues, Zonal Councils are more region-specific and focus on matters of regional development and cooperation.
 
• Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganization Act of 1956, while ISC is a constitutional body provided for under Article 263.
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Commission and ISC:**
 
 
• The Sarkaria Commission, set up in 1983, recommended strengthening the ISC to improve center-state relations.
 
• It emphasized that the ISC should meet at least thrice a year to ensure continuous dialogue and cooperation between the states and the center.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Role Exclusion:**
 
 
• The ISC is not a judicial body and cannot settle disputes between states or between the center and states. Such disputes are adjudicated by the Supreme Court under Article 131 of the Constitution.
